lessons.name: The octet rule: atoms bond to reach eight valence electrons. Carbon has 4 of its own and shares 4 more, 4 + 4 = 8 — a full outer shell, the driver of covalent bonding.
lessons.why: The octet rule: atoms bond to reach eight valence electrons. Carbon has 4 of its own and shares 4 more, 4 + 4 = 8 — a full outer shell, the driver of covalent bonding.

lessons.name: Molar mass sums the atomic masses: water is 2·1 (hydrogen) + 16 (oxygen) = 18 g/mol. The molecule weighs exactly its parts.
lessons.why: Molar mass sums the atomic masses: water is 2·1 (hydrogen) + 16 (oxygen) = 18 g/mol. The molecule weighs exactly its parts.

lessons.name: A Lewis structure counts total valence electrons: H₂O has 2·1 (the hydrogens) + 6 (oxygen) = 8 electrons — four pairs, two bonding and two lone. The dot structure conserves the count.
lessons.why: A Lewis structure counts total valence electrons: H₂O has 2·1 (the hydrogens) + 6 (oxygen) = 8 electrons — four pairs, two bonding and two lone. The dot structure conserves the count.

lessons.name: A covalent bond of order n shares 2n electrons: single, double and triple bonds share 2, 4 and 6 — [1,2,3] → [2,4,6]. The bond IS the shared pair(s).
lessons.why: A covalent bond of order n shares 2n electrons: single, double and triple bonds share 2, 4 and 6 — [1,2,3] → [2,4,6]. The bond IS the shared pair(s).

lessons.name: Main-group valence electrons are the group number minus 10: carbon (group 14) has 4, oxygen (group 16) has 6 — 14 − 10 = 4 and 16 − 10 = 6. Valence count sets how many bonds an atom forms.
lessons.why: Main-group valence electrons are the group number minus 10: carbon (group 14) has 4, oxygen (group 16) has 6 — 14 − 10 = 4 and 16 − 10 = 6. Valence count sets how many bonds an atom forms.

lessons.name: A large electronegativity difference makes a bond ionic: NaCl has |3.0 − 0.9| = 2.1 (×10: 30 − 9 = 21), above the ~1.7 (×10: 17) ionic threshold — 21 > 17. The more electronegative atom takes the electron outright.
lessons.why: A large electronegativity difference makes a bond ionic: NaCl has |3.0 − 0.9| = 2.1 (×10: 30 − 9 = 21), above the ~1.7 (×10: 17) ionic threshold — 21 > 17. The more electronegative atom takes the electron outright.

lessons.name: Bond order is (bonding − antibonding)/2: N₂ gets (8−2)/2 = 3 (a triple bond) and O₂ gets (8−4)/2 = 2 (a double bond). Nitrogen holds three shared pairs, oxygen two.
